## Overview 

For the **XH** component, the `SIS` module implements a generalized version of the *S-I-S* compartmental model both

1. as a system of ordinary differential equations; and

```{r}
library(ramp.xds)
ode_mod <- xds_setup(XHname = "SIS") 
```

```{r, echo=F}
#devtools::load_all()
```

2. as a discrete time system.

```{r}
dts_mod <- xds_setup(XHname = "SIS", xds= "dts") 
```

 This vignette describes the basic model and its generalized implementation in **`ramp.xds.`**

### The Basic S-I-S model 

In the S-I-S model, individuals are either infected and infectious $(I)$ or uninfected and susceptible to infection $(S)$, and the total population sizes is $H=S+I.$

The rate that susceptible individuals become infected is called the *force of infection* (or FoI, Ross called it the *happenings* rate, denoted $h$). The rate of clearance is $r.$ After clearing an infection, individuals are susceptible to infection again. In its simplest form.  

$$
\begin{array}{rl}
\frac{dS}{dt} &= - h S + r I \\
\frac{dI}{dt} &=  h S - r I \\
\end{array}
$$
For this system, note that $$\frac{dS}{dt} = - \frac{dI}{dt}$$ and since $H=S+I,$ we can compute $$\frac{dH}{dt} = \frac{dS}{dt} + \frac{dI}{dt} = 0.$$ In this case, $H$ is a parameter, and we don't need to compute both variables. We could simply compute: 

$$
\frac{dI}{dt} =  h (H-I) - r I 
$$

This is the system that is implemented for the *default* parameter settings.

### Demographic Change

In **`ramp.xds`** we implement a generalized approach to the demographic processes: the system includes births $B$ and deaths (in this case, at the per-capita rate $\mu$), now $H$ is a variable, and we can write out full dynamical system for all three variables. We write it to emphasize the two parts: disease dynamics (**X**) and human population dynamics (**H**): 

$$
\begin{array}{rcc}
& \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{H} \\ \hline 
\frac{dH}{dt} =& & B(t,H) - \mu H \\
\frac{dS}{dt} =& - h S + r I  & + B(t,H) - \mu S  \\
\frac{dI}{dt} =&  h S - r I &- \mu I \\
\end{array}
$$
Since $H=S+I,$ one of these equations is redundant. To implement *progressive stratification,* we drop $S,$ and use a function $\mathbf{D}$ that computes deaths for some variable in a consistent way:

$$
\begin{array}{rcr}
\frac{dH}{dt} =& &B(t,H) - \mathbf{D}(t,H)\\
\frac{dI}{dt} =&  h (H-I) - r I &- \mathbf{D}(t,I)\\
\end{array}
$$
After solving, we compute $S=H+I$ and attach its orbit. By default, birth rates and death rates are set to zero, a constant population model, equivalent to the basis S-I-S model.  The birth and death functions are modified using:

+ [setup_births](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/reference/setup_births.html)

+ [setup_deaths](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/reference/setup_deaths.html)

### Treatment 

In the S-I-S model, there is no chemoprotected state, so drug taking simply clears infections. (In other models, a brief period of chemo-protection follows treatment.) The module assumes that 

+ $\rho$ or `rho`: a fraction $\rho$ of incident infections are treated and cured, so the FoI is now $h (1-\rho).$ Since exposure and infection could also occur in folks who are uninfected, infected individuals also clear at the additional rate $\rho h.$

+ $\sigma$ or `sigma`: treatment and curing also occurs for other reasons at the rate $\sigma.$ 

+ $\Xi(t)$: mass treatment is implemented either as mass drug administration (`mda(t)`) or mass screening and treating (`msat(t)`), a shock function $\Xi(t)$ 

+ The total rate that infections clear is thus: 
$$r + \rho h + \sigma + \Xi(t)$$ 

By default, treatment probabilities and rates are set to zero, so it is equivalent to the basis S-I-S model.

## Dynamics 

### ODE 

For the system of ordinary differential equations, the system is: 

$$
\begin{array}{rcc}
& \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{H} \\ \hline 
\frac{dH}{dt} =& &B(t,H) - \mathbf{D}(t,H)\\
\frac{dI}{dt} =&  h (1-\rho)(H-I) - \left(r + h\rho + \sigma + \Xi \left( t \right) \right) I &- \mathbf{D}(t,I)\\
\end{array}
$$

### DTS 

In the discrete-time system, the demographic change for $I_t$ is computed in two steps: survival $(I_s)$ and then infection dynamics:

$$
\begin{array}{rcc}
& \mathbf{X} & \mathbf{H} \\ \hline 
H_{t+1} =& &B(t,H_t) - \mathbf{D}(t,H_t)\\
I_s  =& & I_t -  \mathbf{D}(t,I_t) \\  
I_{t+1} &= \alpha_t(1-\rho) (H_{t+1} + I_s) + e^{-\left(r + h\rho + \sigma + \Xi \left( t \right) \right)} I_s \\
\end{array}
$$




## Exposure 

The module handles exposure through the standard interface (see [Exposure](Exposure.html)). In a nutshell: 

+ $E(t)$: the daily EIR is computed for each population stratum 

+ $b$ is a basis prameter in the **SIS** module describing the probability of getting infected by an infectious bite 

+ $h$ is the daily FoI, `foi` (or what Ross called the *happenings* rate): 

    - it is computed in `Exposure` as $h = F_h(b, E)$ 

    - By default, the FoI assumes the number of bites per persion is Poisson, so the FoI is linearly proportional to the EIR: $h = b E$ 
    
For more, including advanced setup options, see [Exposure](Exposure.html]) 
    
## Infectiousness: $c$  

Infected humans are not fully infectious. We assume that the fraction of bloodmeals on infectious humans that infect a mosquito is $c.$ The blood feeding and transmission interface uses biting weights and availability, so we compute the infectious density of a stratum: $$F_I = c I.$$

If there is a single population stratum, then  
$$\kappa = \frac {cI} H$$

## Diagnostics and Detection 

Test positivity is denoted $q$, so while true prevalence is $$x=I/H,$$ observed prevalence is $$x_q=qI/H.$$ The model uses a single parameter, `q`, and does not distinguish detection by light microscopy, RDT, or PCR.

`F_pr_obs.SIS` computes observed prevalence. After solving, use
`get_PR(mod, method = "obs")` to retrieve it. The SIS methods for
`F_pfpr_by_lm`, `F_pfpr_by_rdt`, and `F_pfpr_by_pcr` remain compatibility
aliases and return the same observed prevalence using `q`.

We note that in this model, the observed PR is a linear function of the true PR. 
The skill set reports `pr_obs = TRUE` and `pf_lm = pf_rdt = pf_pcr = FALSE`.

## Basic Setup


### Variables

During basic setup, the defaults are 

+ `H=1000` 

+ `I=1` 

### Parameters 

During basic setup, the parameters are assigned the following default values:  

+ `b=0.55` 

+ `r=1/180` 

+ `c=0.15` 

+ `rho=0` 

+ `sigma=0` 

+ `q=0.8`

To inspect the parameters, use `get_XH_pars.` We already set up `mod` using the default values:

```{r}
get_XH_pars(ode_mod)$r
```

To override the defaults at setup, pass a named list to  `xds_setup.` 

```{r}
mod1 <- xds_setup(XHname = "SIS", XHoptions = list(r=1/200))
get_XH_pars(mod1)$r
```

To change a parameter value after setup, pass a named list to  `change_XH_pars.` 


```{r}
ode_mod <- change_XH_pars(ode_mod, options = list(r=1/100))
get_XH_pars(ode_mod)$r
```

*** 

## Mass Treatment 

The module includes a port to simulate mass treatment. In the SIS model, mass treatment increases the clearance rate from $r$ to  $r + \xi(t)$. After curing an infection, in this model, the humans become susceptible to infection again. 

$$
\dot{I} = h (H-I)  - \left(r+\xi\left(t\right)\right) I
$$


$\Xi(t)$ includes both `mda(t)` and `msat(t)`: functions implementing mass treatment

- The function `mda(t)` implements mass drug administration
    
- The function `msat(t)` implements mass screen and treat using detection parameters (see above) 

During basic set up, the function returns no effect: `mda(t)=msat(t)=0`.  Configuring a mass treatment function is handled as an advanced setup option in `ramp.control` (see [`ramp.control`::Mass Treatment](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.control/articles/MassTreatment.html))

    
+ [ramp.forcing;:setup_mass_treatment)


## Example 

Here we run a simple example with 3 population strata at equilibrium. We use `ramp.xds::setup_XH` to set up parameters, and `ramp.xds::setup_XH_inits` to set the initial values. We configure a `trace` function to force the EIR. 

Users interested in more technical details should read [our fully worked multi-patch example](ex_534.html). 

First, we define the size of three population strata:

```{r}
H <- c(100, 500, 250)
nStrata <- length(H) 
``` 

We use the use the default model of human demography with no births or deaths. 

Next, we define the parameter values for all three strata as a named list:

```{r}
b <- rep(0.55, nStrata) 
c <- rep(0.15, nStrata) 
r <- rep(1/200, nStrata)
```

To use these values to build our model, we create a named list:

```{r}
Xo = list(b=b, c=c, r=r)
```

We want to set up the model in a way that tests the software. We want to set values of the EIR and, knowing what the answer should be, show that we get them back.  First, we set the values of the FoI, and then we compute the EIR:

```{r}
foi = c(1:3)/365 
eir <- foi/b 
```

The equilibrium values we should get back after running the equations to steady state are $I = H h /(h+r)$

```{r}
I_eq = H*foi/(foi+r) 
I_eq
```



First, we use `xds_setup` and next, we do it the long way 

## Using Setup 

To set up the model, we simply do this:  

```{r}
xds_setup_eir(eir, XHname="SIS", HPop=H, XHoptions = Xo) -> test_SIS_ode
xds_setup_eir(eir, XHname="SIS", HPop=H, XHoptions = Xo, xds="dts") -> test_SIS_dts
```

To solve it, we do this:

```{r}
xds_solve(test_SIS_ode)-> test_SIS_ode
xds_solve(test_SIS_dts)-> test_SIS_dts
``` 

We plot the prevalence over time: 

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
clrs = viridisLite::turbo(5)[c(1,2,5)]
xds_plot_PR(test_SIS_ode, clr=clrs)
xds_plot_PR(test_SIS_dts, lty=2, clrs = rep("orange", 3), add=T)
```

If we set the initial values of $I$ to the steady state values, the variables  shouldn't change at all. To change the values, we simply add them to the list

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
test_SIS <- change_XH_inits(test_SIS_ode, options = list(I=I_eq))
xds_solve(test_SIS)-> test_SIS 
xds_plot_PR(test_SIS, clr=clrs)
```

Or we can use the `get_XH_orbits` function to get the values of the orbits. This gets the return values and pulls of the the values of $I$ at the last time step: 

```{r}
get_XH_orbits(test_SIS, 1) -> XH2
I_last <- tail(XH2$I, 1)
I_last
``` 

```{r}
sum(tail(XH2$I, 1) - I_eq)
```

## Another Test

If we set $I(0) = 0$, the simple model has a closed form solution: 

$$
I(t) = H (1-e^{-(h+r) t}) \frac{h}{h+r}
$$
We can reset the initial conditions and solve the system of differential equations: 

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
test_SIS <- change_XH_inits(test_SIS, options = list(I=rep(0,3)))
xds_solve(test_SIS)-> test_SIS 
Itest = get_XH_orbits(test_SIS, 1)$I 
xds_plot_PR(test_SIS, clr=clrs)
```

...and we can compute the exact solutions for the same values of $t$: 

```{r}
t = get_XH_orbits(test_SIS, 1)$time
It = matrix(0, 366, 3)
ss = H*foi/(r+foi)
for(i in 1:3){
  It[,i] = H[i]*(1-exp(-(r[i]+foi[i])*t))*foi[i]/(foi[i]+r[i])
}
```

The summing over all the squared differences is less than $10^{-6}.$ 

```{r}
sum((It-Itest)^2) < 1e-6
```
